Question 5(d) [12 marks]: What does art reveal about society in New Kingdom Egypt during this period?
Support your response using evidence from relevant sources.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
10–12 marks: Provides an informed explanation of what art reveals about society during this period | Demonstrates detailed knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Integrates evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates effectively using a range of appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Provides an explanation of what art reveals about society during this period | Demonstrates knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Uses evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates using appropriate terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Provides some understanding of what art reveals about society | Demonstrates some knowledge relevant to the question | Refers to one or more sources in the response | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and concepts
1–3 marks: Makes general statement(s) about society/an aspect of society | May refer to source(s) | May use historical terms and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Art reveals much about religion in New Kingdom Egypt in this period. For example, tomb decorations, such as those in the Valley of the Kings, detail much about Egyptian beliefs regarding the journey to the afterlife.
• Art in tomb decoration reveals details regarding clothing, leisure, diet, daily life and work in this period.
• Art reveals details regarding the desired image of the pharaoh in this period, such as the famous smiting scenes of Thutmose III from Karnak which emphasise the military might of pharaoh.
• Art reveals information regarding trade and the impact of empire in this period. For example, the reliefs at Deir el-Bahri regarding the journey to Punt under Hatshepsut, show some of the materials accumulated from this trip, including incense trees. Reliefs regarding Thutmose III’s various campaigns to Syria-Palestine, such as those at Karnak, depict the booty gathered, including chariots and precious stones.
• Art also reveals information regarding the army, its weaponry and practices. Depiction of bows, spears and chariots are prominent. There is also the depiction of looting after battle, such as the scenes of Thutmose III’s Battle of Megiddo.
